title: Installing trust
summary: Make Linux, Windows, Docker images and every runtime trust your private root, and know which store each one reads.

steps.title: Linux: add a root to the system store
body: sudo cp dojo-root.pem /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/dojo-root.crt   # PEM content, .crt name!
trust list | grep -i dojo              # check it is there

Install only **roots** (or your own issuing CA if that's the anchor you want), never leaf certificates. Check the file first: `openssl x509 -in dojo-root.pem -noout -subject -ext basicConstraints` should say `CA:TRUE`.

steps.explain: Check it is a CA, copy with a `.crt` name, rebuild the bundle, then prove it with a client that uses the system store.
Debian-family and Red Hat-family use different folders and different commands. Mixing them up is the classic "it said done but nothing changed".

steps.title: Windows and Docker
body: # every user on the machine (run as administrator)
certutil -addstore -f Root corp-root.cer          # same thing, from cmd
GUI: `certlm.msc` (machine) and `certmgr.msc` (user) â†’ Trusted Root Certification Authorities â†’ Certificates. Group Policy pushes roots to a whole domain.
**Docker:** a container has its own filesystem, so the host's trust store does not apply. Bake the root into the image:
(Alpine images may need `RUN apk add --no-cache ca-certificates` first.)

steps.title: Which store does each runtime read?
body: Installing a root in the OS store fixes **some** programs. Others carry their own list:
| Runtime | Trust store it uses | Add your root |
| .NET on Linux | OpenSSL's system store (`/etc/ssl/certs`) | `update-ca-certificates`; or `SSL_CERT_FILE` / `SSL_CERT_DIR` |
| curl, wget, git | system bundle | system store; or `curl --cacert`, `CURL_CA_BUNDLE`, `git config http.sslCAInfo` |
| Node.js | its **own built-in** Mozilla list | `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/path/corp-root.pem` (read at start-up) |
| Go | system store | system store; or `SSL_CERT_FILE` |
`REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` and `SSL_CERT_FILE` **replace** the default list, so point them at the full system bundle (which now includes your root), not at your root alone.

steps.prompt: Match each runtime to how you add a private root for it.
After `update-ca-certificates`, `curl https://intranet.corp.example` works, but a Python script using `requests` still fails with `CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED`. Why?
options: The root must be in DER format for Python
steps.explain: Different runtime, different store. Pointing `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` at the system bundle makes Python agree with curl.

steps.prompt: You copied `corp-root.pem` to `/usr/local/share/ca-certificates/` and `update-ca-certificates` printed `0 added, 0 removed`. Why?
options: The file must be named `*.crt`; rename it to `corp-root.crt`
steps.explain: Debian's tool only picks up `.crt` files in that folder (PEM content, `.crt` name).

steps.prompt: A trust bundle is just PEM blocks one after another. What does this print?
code: var a = DojoCert("CN=Public Root A", null, true);
var b = DojoCert("CN=Public Root B", null, true);
var corp = DojoCert("CN=Corp Root CA", null, true);

string bundle = "# ca-certificates.crt
" + a.ExportCertificatePem() + "
" + b.ExportCertificatePem() + "
" + corp.ExportCertificatePem() + "
";
static X509Certificate2 DojoCert(string subject, X509Certificate2? issuer, bool isCa, string? dns = null, string? eku = null, int nbYear = 2030, int naYear = 2035)
var req = new CertificateRequest(subject, key, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256);
req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509KeyUsageExtension(isCa ? X509KeyUsageFlags.KeyCertSign | X509KeyUsageFlags.CrlSign : X509KeyUsageFlags.DigitalSignature, true));
if (dns != null) { var b = new SubjectAlternativeNameBuilder(); foreach (var d in dns.Split(',')) b.AddDnsName(d); req.CertificateExtensions.Add(b.Build()); }
if (eku != null) req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509EnhancedKeyUsageExtension(new OidCollection { new Oid(eku) }, false));
using var pub = req.Create(issuer, nb, na, serial);
steps.explain: That is all `/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt` is: `update-ca-certificates` concatenates every trusted root into one file.

steps.title: Trust from a bundle, like SSL_CERT_FILE
prompt: Write `bool TrustsWithBundle(string bundlePem, X509Certificate2 leaf, X509Certificate2Collection intermediates)`: does a client whose trust store is the PEM bundle `bundlePem` (what `SSL_CERT_FILE` points at) accept `leaf`?
- load every certificate in the bundle as a trust anchor (`CustomRootTrust`)
starter: bool TrustsWithBundle(string bundlePem, X509Certificate2 leaf, X509Certificate2Collection intermediates)
solution: bool TrustsWithBundle(string bundlePem, X509Certificate2 leaf, X509Certificate2Collection intermediates)
hints: `ImportFromPem` the bundle into a collection, then `CustomTrustStore.AddRange(...)`.
template: var dojoRoot = DojoCert("CN=Corp Root CA", null, true, naYear: 2040);
var dojoInt = DojoCert("CN=Corp Issuing CA", dojoRoot, true);
var dojoA = DojoCert("CN=Public Root A", null, true);
Dojo.Eq("public bundle only: not trusted", false, TrustsWithBundle(dojoPublicOnly, dojoLeaf, dojoInts));
Dojo.Eq("bundle with the corp root: trusted", true, TrustsWithBundle(dojoWithCorp, dojoLeaf, dojoInts));
Dojo.Eq("corp root but no intermediate: not trusted", false, TrustsWithBundle(dojoWithCorp, dojoLeaf, new X509Certificate2Collection()));
Dojo.Eq("a clientAuth certificate is not accepted as a server", false, TrustsWithBundle(dojoWithCorp, dojoClient, dojoInts));
static X509Certificate2 DojoCert(string subject, X509Certificate2? issuer, bool isCa, string? dns = null, string? eku = null, int nbYear = 2030, int naYear = 2035)
var req = new CertificateRequest(subject, key, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256);
req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509KeyUsageExtension(isCa ? X509KeyUsageFlags.KeyCertSign | X509KeyUsageFlags.CrlSign : X509KeyUsageFlags.DigitalSignature, true));
if (dns != null) { var b = new SubjectAlternativeNameBuilder(); foreach (var d in dns.Split(',')) b.AddDnsName(d); req.CertificateExtensions.Add(b.Build()); }
if (eku != null) req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509EnhancedKeyUsageExtension(new OidCollection { new Oid(eku) }, false));
